subject: Billing channel favorability — PO vs virtual card for trial
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Harper <evan@lyramed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Billing channel favorability — PO vs virtual card for trial

Thanks for the time today, Evan — quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Call highlights:
- Pilot scope: 6-week evaluation (chat + embeddings) for LyraMed product ops team, estimated spend ~$18–25k for pilot period.
- Primary constraint: AP requires a vendor onboarding packet plus either a standard PO process or virtual card for payment.
- Marketplace option: team is open to marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace) if it reduces procurement friction, but wants to understand pricing parity and lead time.

Key questions we need to resolve to move to a signed pilot:
1) Which billing channel will be preferred by AP — official PO or virtual card? Any thresholds (e.g., <$X on card)?
2) Who owns vendor onboarding paperwork at LyraMed (procurement contact + email)?
3) If marketplace purchase is preferred, can you share the marketplace admin contact or portal link?
4) Any other legal/finance blockers (tax forms, custom invoicing cadence)?

Next steps (proposed):
- Evan: share vendor onboarding packet requirements and AP contact (by EOD Thu).
- Mina: attach draft SOW and supplier packet for their intake (sent now), flag option to accept virtual card for pilot to speed execution.
- Karthik/Marissa: stand by for procurement sync if LyraMed needs pricing addendum for PO.

Attachments: [LyraMed_SupplierPacket.pdf (application/pdf)] — this is a single-page supplier checklist we typically send to AP to pre-fill.

If a virtual card is acceptable for the pilot we can cut the timeline from ~3 weeks to ~3 business days (vendor setup + charge). Otherwise, we’ll align on PO lead time and prepare SOW + invoice cadence for their finance process.

Would appreciate the AP contact and any note on card thresholds so we can recommend the cleanest path.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Evan Harper <evan@lyramed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing channel favorability — PO vs virtual card for trial

Thanks, Mina — good summary and appreciate the template. Quick answers from AP side:
- Preference: PO is our standard for recurring vendors. For one-off pilots under $50k we can accept virtual/virtual-card payments if procurement and legal sign off.
- Thresholds: Virtual card is typically used for invoices <$50k; anything above needs a PO and vendor onboarding completed.
- Paperwork: procurement@lyramed.com is the intake mailbox. They require: vendor W9 (if US entity), supplier packet, and a short risk questionnaire.
- Marketplace: we use AWS Marketplace for a subset of purchases. Marketplace requires listing parity (same SKU/pricing) and a contract uploaded to their system; that can add 7–10 business days.

I attached the most recent supplier packet and W9 template we use — fills the fields our AP team expects.

Attachment references: [LyraMed_W9.pdf (application/pdf)], [LyraMed_Supplier_Onboarding_Instructions.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Evan

Director of Procurement, LyraMed

Perfect, thanks for the clarity — that helps a lot. Two quick notes and proposed timeline:

1) Vendor packet + W9: I27m attaching our SOW draft and a short vendor intake we ask customers to complete; feel free to forward both to procurement@lyramed.com. If they want us to complete anything directly we can.

Attachments: [Redwood_SOW_DRAFT.pdf (application/pdf)]

2) Recommended paths based on your thresholds:
- Fast path (recommended for pilot): LyraMed accepts a virtual card (<$50k) — we can provision access and invoice within 3 business days after procurement confirms card routing.
- Standard path: Complete vendor onboarding + PO issuance — estimated 7–14 business days depending on procurement backlog and legal review.
- Marketplace path: Use AWS Marketplace — additional ~7–10 business days; good for longer-term procurement and consolidated billing.

3) Ask: Can procurement@lyramed.com confirm the person who will receive the supplier packet and an expected SLA for vendor onboarding? That will help us coordinate finance and support resources.

4) If helpful, we can have our partner ops (Marissa) join a short 15-minute call with your procurement lead to expedite setup (we can share a checklist live).

Proposed next step: Evan, please reply with procurement contact and whether you27d like us to send a card-based invoice for the POC. If yes, I27ll send the card payment request and our team will stand by for the charge confirmation.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to an executed pilot.

Best,
